title: KaDeWe Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **KaDeWe is Berlin's grand old department store, and its food hall is the real reason to go.** Kaufhaus des Westens, "the department store of the west," has been open since 1907 and is the largest department store in continental Europe. Fashion fills most of it, but the sixth-floor food hall is what pulls travellers in.

**Where and when.** Tauentzienstraße 21 to 24, in the former West Berlin, with the U-Bahn stop **Wittenbergplatz** (U1, U2, U3) right outside. It opens roughly **Monday to Saturday, 10:00 to 20:00, and is closed on Sundays** like almost every shop in Germany.

**The 6th-floor food hall is free to walk into.** Around 35 counters, from an oyster and champagne bar to cheese, chocolate and a whole hall of pastries. You do not have to buy anything, and you can eat standing up at the counters.
**One floor higher is the 7th-floor Winter Garden**, a rooftop food court under a glass roof with a view over Wittenbergplatz. It is the calmer place to actually sit down and eat.

**It is a west-Berlin landmark, not part of the historic centre.** KaDeWe is a long way from Alexanderplatz and the Museum Island side of the city, so treat it as its own half-day rather than something you pass on the way to everything else.

**Practical bits.** No entry fee, cards are accepted everywhere, and non-EU visitors can ask about tax-free shopping. Go mid-morning or later in the afternoon to dodge the lunch crush on the sixth floor.
